title: Registration Fee Exemptions 2026: Self-Built Homes, New Certificates
desc: Self-built homes, replaced or reissued certificates, divided marital property, resettlement and poor households are exempt from registration fees.
summary: Lesser-known cases of exemption from the real estate registration fee under Consolidated Document 33/VBHN-BTC: self-built homes, reissued certificates, resettlement, poor households, and deferred fees.
body: p

The registration fee on real estate is 0.5% when registering ownership or use rights (Article 8 of Consolidated Document 33/VBHN-BTC). The article Registration fee on real estate 2026 covered how it is calculated and the exemption for gifts and inheritance between relatives. This article gathers the other exemptions in Article 10 that homeowners often overlook.
h2
1. Self-built houses of households and individuals
p

Exempt from the registration fee are houses of households and individuals created through detached housing development under the Housing Law (Clause 11, Article 10). When a newly built house is completed and registered on the Certificate (land use right certificate, sổ đỏ), the self-built house qualifies for exemption. For the procedure, see As-built completion and registering a house on the land use right certificate 2026.
h2
2. Replacing, reissuing, or re-registering a Certificate
p
For property that already has a Certificate, re-registration is exempt in these cases (Clause 16, Article 10):
ul
A Certificate issued by a competent authority (including under the former regime) that is now exchanged for a new one without a change of owner.

Common household property divided among members and re-registered; property merged between spouses after marriage; property divided between husband and wife on divorce under a court judgment or decision.
Reissuance because the certificate was lost, torn, or damaged: no exemption procedure needs to be declared.
Reissuance with additional area but with the plot boundary unchanged: the additional area is exempt.
Re-registration because of a change in land use purpose without a change of land user and without having to pay land use fees.
h2
3. Agricultural land and leased land
ul

Land allocated, leased, or recognized by the State for agricultural, forestry, aquaculture, or salt production (Clause 4); self-reclaimed agricultural land consistent with the plan, undisputed, and issued a Certificate (Clause 6).
Land leased from the State with annual rent, or leased from a person with lawful land use rights (Clause 7).
h2
4. Resettlement, charity houses, poor households
ul

Houses and land received as compensation or resettlement, including houses and land bought with compensation or support money when the State recovers land; applies to the person whose land was recovered (Clause 15).
Charity houses, solidarity houses, and houses given as humanitarian support, including the attached land, registered in the name of the recipient (Clause 20).
Houses and residential land of poor households; of households and individuals in areas with difficult or especially difficult socio-economic conditions (Clause 26).
h2
5. Contributing real estate as capital to a business
p

An individual who has already paid the registration fee and now contributes capital to a business or cooperative using their house and land: the business registering it is exempt (Point a, Clause 17, Article 10).
h2
6. If you do not have the money yet: deferral is possible
p

Households and individuals eligible to have land use fees deferred may also defer the registration fee; the Certificate is marked "Registration fee owed". When repaying, the fee is paid based on the house and land price at the time of declaration. Before transferring or gifting to others, the outstanding amount must be paid in full, except for gifts between relatives (Article 9).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. Decree 202/2026/ND-CP (effective 1 March 2027) amends only the rules on electric cars and does not change the exemptions above. Exemptions are determined by the tax authority on declaration; it is advisable to ask the Land Registration Office or the tax authority where the property is located.
